clue.text: Lobs my distorted logo

indicators.note: something distorted is twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tosses up a badly warped company emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: A logo is an emblem or sign standing for a company, which is a kind of symbol.

clue.text: Keep about 50 for something soothing

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: to keep is to save
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Store up roughly fifty jars of something calming.
explanation.definitionFit: A salve is an ointment that relieves pain, so it is a soothing remedy.

clue.text: Raincoat man found in tarry surface

parts.note: a mac (mackintosh) is a raincoat
Adam, the first man in Genesis

explanation.surface: A man in a raincoat is discovered lying on a tar-covered road.
explanation.definitionFit: Macadam is road surfacing of broken stone, often bound with tar.

clue.text: Clothier is away, getting healthier

parts.note: someone who is out is away from home
fitter means in better health

explanation.surface: A tailor goes off on a break and comes back in better shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter is a shop or trader selling clothes, the same trade as a clothier.

clue.text: Fathead put high explosive on deck

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a clot is a fool, a fathead

explanation.surface: An idiot sets explosives on a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' looks like a ship's floor, but it is the verb, as in 'deck out'.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck someone out is to dress or adorn them, a synonym of clothe.

clue.text: Textile machinery seems very close

definitions.meaning: something that ... appears large and imminent

explanation.definitionFit: Looms are weaving machines, and to loom is to appear close and threatening.

clue.text: Welshman endlessly fed up with silk

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: Taffy is a traditional nickname for a Welshman

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word is read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to have fed is to have eaten

explanation.surface: A Welshman, sick of it all, is stuck with a silk garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed up' looks like 'annoyed', but it splits: fed is the piece, 'up' the reversal signal, reading it bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp woven fabric, traditionally made of silk.

clue.text: Go in with a tin perhaps and amuse

parts.note: to go in is to enter

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible variant, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Walk in carrying a tin and keep everyone entertained.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain guests is to amuse them.

clue.text: A time and place outside to pacify

indicators.note: outside means one piece goes round the other

explanation.surface: Somewhere to calm people down, with an hour and a venue set.
explanation.definitionFit: To placate someone is to calm their anger, a synonym of pacify.

clue.text: Disprove chief engineer has grabbed new futon

indicators.note: something grabbed is held inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: CE is the abbreviation for chief engineer

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A chief engineer seizes a new futon to disprove something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges the futon's letters, and 'has grabbed' sets them between C and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To confute an argument is to prove it wrong, a formal synonym of disprove.

clue.text: Myriapod ruined decent pie

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A perfectly decent pie has been spoilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A centipede is a many-legged arthropod, one of the myriapods.

clue.text: Put time limits on Sweden-a very boring state

indicators.note: in an across answer, a piece put on another follows it

parts.note: deadlines are time limits
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: Imposing deadlines on Sweden makes for a tedious existence.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly can mean extremely dull, so deadliness is the condition of being very boring.

clue.text: Lear upset member of nobility

indicators.note: upset means overturned or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: King Lear is upset by one of his nobles.
explanation.walkthrough: Lear is Shakespeare's king, which makes the noble surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British peer ranking above a viscount.

clue.text: Arrive on time in this plane

indicators.note: in an across answer, a piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: to come is to arrive

explanation.surface: Travellers land punctually on this aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: The de Havilland Comet was the first jet airliner.
explanation.definitionFit: The Comet was a British jet airliner of the 1950s, so a plane by name.

clue.text: Rejoice in famous person's fee?

parts.note: a celeb is a famous person (celebrity)
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: A celebrity is delighted with the size of their appearance fee.
explanation.definitionFit: To celebrate is to mark an occasion with joy, a synonym of rejoice.

clue.text: Remove food in two parts

definitions.meaning: to remove is to carry off
a ready-cooked meal bought to eat elsewhere

explanation.walkthrough: 'In two parts' points to the (4,4) split: a verb phrase in one sense, a single noun in the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Take away means remove, and a takeaway is a meal bought ready-cooked to eat elsewhere.

clue.text: Kelvin at present is on the shelf, learning

parts.note: K is the symbol for the kelvin unit of temperature
now means at present
a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: Lord Kelvin, these days, has been left on the shelf despite all his learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge is what is gained by learning; the two are synonyms for acquired understanding.

clue.text: Applaud section going back for rubbish

parts.note: to clap is to applaud

indicators.note: going back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a part is a section

explanation.surface: An audience claps one passage and then returns for more nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious nonsense, talk that amounts to rubbish.

clue.text: A hobby for Fathers' Day, perhaps?

parts.note: pas are fathers, so fathers' is the possessive pas'
a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a hobby to take up on Fathers' Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' flags that Day for time is a loose example; the whimsical reading is the time belonging to dads.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastime is an activity done for pleasure, which is a hobby.

clue.text: Constellation or something charged

parts.note: an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: A star pattern, or perhaps something electrically charged.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion, the hunter, is a prominent constellation.

clue.text: Draws in originally towards the middle

indicators.note: originally points to the words before they were rearranged, so the answer is a rearrangement of them

explanation.surface: Something pulls inward, as it was first designed to.
explanation.definitionFit: Inwards means in a direction toward the inside or centre.

clue.text: Bird is the same in front

indicators.note: in front means the first piece goes before the second

parts.note: ib is short for ibidem, Latin for 'in the same place', used in references

explanation.surface: A bird is identical to the one leading.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a curved bill.

clue.text: Drunk to win a thousand with game counter

parts.note: tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk
K stands for a thousand, as in kilo

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy hopes to win a thousand pounds with a gaming chip.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiddlywink is one of the small plastic discs flicked in the game tiddlywinks.

clue.text: Article inside is about number

indicators.note: the article has the next piece inside it

parts.note: the is the definite article
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A piece of writing contains something concerning a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Three is a cardinal number.

clue.text: No and yes, strangely curious

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters are oddly rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps answering no and yes seems oddly inquisitive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' rearranges only YES into SEY; NO stays put at the front, and 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosey means inquisitive, prying into others' business.

clue.text: I carve a cooked hors d'oeuvre

indicators.note: cooked suggests the ingredients are worked up into something new, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook slices up a starter.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviare, salted sturgeon roe, is a classic delicacy served as an hors d'oeuvre.

clue.text: Where one lives in modern times, with something to wear

parts.note: AD (anno Domini) marks the modern era of dating
a dress is a garment

explanation.surface: Someone's home nowadays comes with a fresh outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is the details of the place where a person lives.

clue.text: In Spain, the 50-50 number

parts.note: el is the Spanish for 'the'
fifty-fifty odds are even

explanation.surface: A Spaniard announces a number that is an even chance.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleven is a cardinal number.

clue.text: He became a sly person, mean at heart

indicators.note: at heart means the letters are found in the middle of the phrase

explanation.surface: A man turned into a cunning individual, nasty underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Measly means miserly or pitifully small, a sense of mean.
